name: manual_aad992
claim: When judging whether a detached/orphaned commit represents at-risk unmerged work, ancestor and tree-identity checks alone are insufficient -- content can be fully 'already landed' via an entirely different, independently-derived commit path (convergent evolution, not a literal merge of that branch), which those checks would miss and wrongly flag as still at risk. Verify via git cherry <target> <candidate> <merge-base> (patch-id equivalence per commit) AND, for generated/graduated artifacts with stable content IDs, direct ID lookups against the target.

decisions.notes: Investigated a detached commit (404d3001, kimi-meta-remediation branch) that 'git merge-base --is-ancestor' and a full tree-diff scan both said was NOT already on main. But git cherry showed all 6 unique commits patch-equivalent-absent yet content-wise, checking the 10 actual lesson-candidate IDs individually against main's lessons.jsonl showed all 10 already present -- the real payload had landed through PR #211/#212 via a proper re-graduation, not a merge of this branch. The branch was safe-to-delete bookkeeping, not lost work, but ancestor/tree checks alone would have wrongly suggested otherwise.
